facts.text: Ellenboro got its name in 1884 when Seaboard engineer John Robinson suggested naming the town after his dying daughter, Ellen.
In 1880 the Seaboard Air Line Railroad built a line from Wilmington to Rutherfordton, passing through what would become Ellenboro.
On October 27, 2022 Ellenboro celebrated its heritage by acquiring the historic Colfax Cotton Gin site, preserving a key piece of local industry.
Early July’s Big Days festival once drew crowds from miles around, featuring a steam‑powered merry‑go‑round, sack races, and lemonade served from zinc tubs.
In 1928 A.B. Bushong organized the first Colfax Free Fair at Ellenboro School, showcasing farmers’ canned goods, baked goods, and handicrafts.
Robinson donated a large brass bell to Ellenboro, which hung in the school for years before disappearing after a new building was erected.
